item.title: What's already decided isn't up for debate: determinism in AI workflows
item.description: An AI agent is non-deterministic by design. To make it reliable, you take the decisions that are already made out of the LLM and crystallise them into hooks, scripts and tables. What stays inside the model is bounded execution; the human is who decides.

item.title: Context window: when your AI agent starts forgetting
item.description: The context window is the scarcest resource in AI-augmented development. When your policies, protocols, and sessions grow, the agent starts ignoring instructions. Here is how we fixed it.

item.title: AI will not replace you. But it will multiply you — careful with being zero
item.description: Developers fear AI will take their jobs. History says otherwise. AI is the next abstraction layer — and it multiplies whoever uses it. But you cannot multiply by zero.

item.title: Inside Claude Code: 10 interesting things from analyzing its source code
item.description: The Claude Code source was briefly leaked and someone made a public port. We analyzed it in depth. Here are some useful things to get more out of it as a developer.

item.title: AI Skills: how to give your AI agent verified knowledge it does not have
item.description: Your AI agent does not know what changed in the latest version of the technologies you use. AI Skills fix that: structured, verified documentation optimized for machines. Here is how we build and use them.

item.title: AI-Augmented Development: my real experience working with an AI agent
item.description: I have been working with an AI agent as a development collaborator for months. It is not autocomplete. It is another developer on the team. This is what I have learned.
